title: Where did the frame go?
description:
Turn one frame's profiler events into the rows of a profiler table:

```cpp
struct Event { bool begin; std::string name; double time; };   // time in milliseconds

std::vector<std::string> profileRows(const std::vector<Event>& events);
```

- Walk the events with a stack. A begin starts a zone inside the zone on top of the stack; an end finishes the zone on top (its name will match).
- Zones with the **same name under the same parent** are merged into one row: their totals add up and their call count increases. Merging also merges their children, by name.
- A row's **total** is the sum of its zones' durations; its **self** time is its total minus the totals of its children.
- Rows are listed depth first: a zone, then its children in the order they first appeared, then its next sibling. Each row is two spaces of indentation per level of depth, then:

```
<name> total <t> self <s>
```

  with one decimal place each, followed by ` (<n> calls)` when merged from more than one zone.

```
frame 0..152:  update 10..61 (physics 12..40, think 41..52, think 52..60),  render 61..150

frame total 152.0 self 12.0
  update total 51.0 self 4.0
    physics total 28.0 self 28.0
    think total 19.0 self 19.0 (2 calls)
  render total 89.0 self 89.0
```

An end event with an empty stack, or events left open at the end, make the result the single line `unbalanced events`.
hints: Build a tree of nodes where each child is found by name (create it the first time). The stack holds the node and the start time of each open zone.
